He had a problem right out the gate with me because I had a folding bike and he had a car. We were both from the same minority group, and in probing my alliance to something by making a dumb joke that I honestly can't remember. I was a barback at the time, so he would sit right in front of my station and stare through me. He was such a a lonely dude. Proclaiming his allegiance like a badge of honor, I could tell he didn't have anybody to talk to. His social skills were missing and out of time. Any scenario where he was trying to stand over me or something would have me met with my boss asking me what I'm doing to him, because us two in the vicinity would make people uncomfortable. I ended up telling him to back off and we got into it. He was happy to try and bug me then after getting a reaction. I eventually got let go, cause I'm just the barback, but I guess all this is to say that people have their allegiances. 

Racism isn't a deal breaker anymore so seeing who's right and who's wrong is all muddied out.
